html:
On 11 May 1960 agents of Israel's Mossad seized Adolf Eichmann on a street near Buenos Aires and took him to Israel to stand trial. He had organised the deportation of Jews to the death camps and had lived in Argentina under the name Ricardo Klement since 1950.

The trail began in 1957, when a half-Jewish man in Argentina, Lothar Hermann, wrote that his daughter's boyfriend was Eichmann's son. Fritz Bauer, a prosecutor in Frankfurt, did not trust West German officials and passed the tip to Israel. After Bauer met Mossad chief Isser Harel in 1959, Harel sent a team. They grabbed Eichmann as he came home from the bus, kept him in a safe house, and got him to sign a statement that he agreed to be tried in Israel. On 20 May they flew him out on an El Al plane that had brought Israeli delegates to Argentina's anniversary celebrations.

Prime Minister David Ben-Gurion announced the capture to the Knesset on 23 May. Argentina protested to the UN Security Council, which in June found that the raid had broken its sovereignty, and relations were strained for a time. Most of the world still wanted him tried. The result was the Eichmann trial.
